Messages.Body:
During a game I played the Master card "Protected Resources" which
states:
If this card is in play, another Methuselah cannot bleed you for more
than 2 pool. Burn this card if you successfully bleed another
Methuselah.

However, my prey said that was only meant that each Vampire could not
bleed for more then 2, while I argued that the card used the word
"methuselah" which meant the total bleed from that methuselah for their
turn could not exceed 2 blood. Who is right?

Paul Cecil

Messages.Body:

ceci...@my-deja.com wrote:
> During a game I played the Master card "Protected Resources" which
> states:
> If this card is in play, another Methuselah cannot bleed you for more
> than 2 pool. Burn this card if you successfully bleed another
> Methuselah.
>
> However, my prey said that was only meant that each Vampire could not
> bleed for more then 2, while I argued that the card used the word
> "methuselah" which meant the total bleed from that methuselah for
> their turn could not exceed 2 blood. Who is right?

Unfortunately, your prey is correct. Methuselahs cannot bleed.

The only official errata / ruling / clarification on PR appears below:

Protected Resources - Master (2)
All cards which modify the bleed amount (Telepathic Counter, Threats,
etc.) are applied before Protected Resources' effect. [TOM 19960413]

But, Methuselahs cannot bleed. The effect of the card only
allows each bleed to be no more than 2, but your predator
can still bleed you with 10 minions for 2 each.

The card really helps Vote decks defend against big bleed decks,
but doesn't help any against weenie horde decks.

Carpe Noctem.

Lasombra

Messages.Author: ceci...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
I searched back in Deja.com and found LSJ's response to a past question
on Protected Resources. It was from a thread dated 4/27/99, I have
repeated his answer in whole below.

> Thread: [LSJ] Protected Resources
>> Message 1 of 8

Subject:
Re: [LSJ] Protected Resources
Date:
04/27/1999
Author:
LSJ <vte...@wizards.com>

Save this thread

"Sorrow" <cbo...@apdi.net> wrote:
> Card Text: Protected Resources
> Card Text: Master - 2 pool
> If this card is in play, another Methuselah may not

> bleed you for more than 2 pool. Burn this card if you
> successfully bleed another Methuselah.
>

> Standing Errata/Rulings/Clarifications:

> All cards which modify the bleed amount (Telepathic Counter,
> Threats, etc.) are applied before Protected Resources' effect.

> [TOM 960413]
>
> ---------
> Now let me get to my point - I've read it several times in several
> posts, a few of those by you I'm pretty sure, that this card is
> interpreted that each bleed (action) is reduced to 2 after all
> modifications/reactions are played. For example, using the above
> interpretation, a minion bleeds for 6, it's prey's minion reduces
> by 2 by whatever means then the PR kicks in making it a bleed of 2
> in the end. Is this correct in how the card is interpreted and my
> example of that interpretation?

Well, the bleed is still for the regular amount (4, in this case), but
only 2 pool is burned for that bleed.

> If so, I'm very curious how that interpretation was made. The card
> says: "another Methuselah may not bleed you for more than 2 pool".
> It doesn't say "another _*minion*_ may not bleed you for more than
> 2 pool". However, a methuselah cannot bleed, only his minions can.
> Since it does not reference a minon as an individual but instead
> references a methuselah, who again, cannot bleed, it must mean the
> bleed actions available to the methuselah as a collective. hmmm,
> re-reading the above, I'm not sure it came out right.

Right. It is possible to read it as the following:

* Each other Methuselah, indiviually, cannot have her minions bleed you
for more than 2 pool for the rest of the game (that
is, you will lose no more than 2 pool, total, for all of the bleeds
from each given Methuselah's minions' actions combined
for the rest of the game). Burn this card if one of your minions
successfully bleeds any Methuselah.

> What I'm trying to say is this:
> I as a methuselah, through my minions, bleed my prey who has PR in
> play. Each of my bleeds, through my minions, are for 2. If I have
> 3 minions, then I, another methuselah, bled my prey for 6 on that
> one turn. However, the card text of PR strictly prohibits me,
> another methuselah, for bleeding for more than 2. So either I
> should not have been allowed to perform those other 2 bleeding
> actions or they should have been reduced to 0. Since PR does not
> say "another minion" or "each minion", then I don't see how it
> could have been interpreted that 'each minion's bleed is reduced to
> 2'. Because a meth controls all his minions and because the card
> text specifically says 'another methuselah' it's pretty clear that
> *all* a meth's minions can't bleed for more than 2 and not just
> *each* of a meth's minions.

It seems as if you're wondering why "per turn" isn't part of the
official interpretation. That's easy: the card makes no
reference to any turn. The only two options available for
interpretation (as opposed to errata) are "for the rest of the game"
(as above) and "for each bleed" (as the official interpretation goes).

"For each bleed", besides being the "reasonable" option when compared
to "for the rest of the game", is used in the official
interepretaion as part of the idea of "bleeding for more than 2". That
phrase carries the idea of the bleed action. See Archon
Investigation (that is, you cannot play Archon Investigation on a
minion who has bled you
successfully thrice before and is now bleeding you again. This stems
from the concept of a single actiong in "bleed for X.")

Also, I suspect, the ruling/clarification came to explain what the card
designers had intended when they wrote the card,
even if the card failed to adequately describe the concept.

Like the old "who is the prey of a minion?" question (Jyhad Fame) -
sometimes the card writers introduce notation without
realizing it (thinking that the notation is clear and unambiguous).

--

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Clarified card text:

Protected Resources
Cardtype: Master
Cost: 2 pool
Master. If this card is in play, <you do not burn more than two pool when a
minion bleeds you, regardless of the amount of the bleed>. Burn this card if

you successfully bleed another Methuselah.

This matches the actual card text:

If this card is in play, another Methuselah may not bleed you for more than 2
pool. Burn this card if you successfully bleed another Methuselah.

Since it doesn't say "per game" or "per turn", the implication is that the
limit is "per bleed".

--

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 14 Feb 2000 ravnos...@my-deja.com wrote:
> I disagree entirely. The card specifically states a Methuselah.

However, it does not state a timescale.

"If this card is in play, another Methuselah cannot bleed you for more

than 2 pool. Burn this card if you successfully bleed another Methuselah."

So, is that 2 pool in one bleed? Two pool per turn? Two pool *forever*?
It does not state which. Clearly, any interpretation of it is just that -
an interpretation. In this instance, where the card is wide open, any
interpretation could be valid.

It is the view of the Rules Team, from all previous comments, that the
correct (officially) interpretation is per vampire.

Indeed, were it to be anything else, any deck with bleed in it (be it
weenie bleed, dominate bleed, presence bleed, computer hacking bleed,
whatever) is *severely* curtailed.

--

James Coupe

That's what clarifications from the Rules Team are for - to CLARIFY
what the card meant to say. In some cases, that's what ERRATA is for,
to make even more clear what the card meant to say. There is a
clarification out for PR that states "2 per bleed action."

>action phase the methusela can bleed you for no more then 2 blood if
>this card is in play.

Methuselahs cannot bleed at all, so your interpretation will always be
valid. However, the VAMPIRES that do the bleeding may bleed for no
more than 2 at a time. Well, they MAY, but it will only remove 2 pool
per bleed action.

THINK, man. If you could not be bled for more than 2 per turn, would
you ever be ousted? Not if you built the deck properly. Let's see -
Justicar with OBF/DOM is a good start. Minion Tap/5th for blood gain,
and with OBF you'll never be caught on the 5th. That gives you about
6-8 pool gain PER minion/5th, which will last you 3-4 turns. A 10-cap
with DOM can play Kindred Coercion at will, so you can forget about
ever ousting the guy with votes. Combat defense can be Obedience,
since he's older than any Rush deck. With OBF/DOM he bleeds for 6 per
turn himself at +3 stealth, assuming it's not a +bleeder.

I'm not sure why anyone would WANT to argue that PR meant "no more
than 2 per turn" - it so obviously makes the card broken.

-- Derek

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 14 Feb 2000 ceci...@my-deja.com wrote:
> I am sorry, but in turn I have to disagree. The problem is that the card
> uses the term 'methusela'.

Yes, but it still could have been written in three ways:

1) This methuselah may not be bled for more than 2 per action.
2) This methuselah may not be bled for more than 2 per turn.
3) This methuselah may not be bled for more than 2 per game.

The ruling is consistent with 1).

If you wish to assert the supremacy of the word Methuselah, may I ask why
you are limiting to it "per turn" (example 2). If one limits it in that
fashion, option 3) is more intuitive by card text - and clearly the most
powerful, by far.

--

James Coupe

Okay, I see where we have gone with this. The "time limit" is the
question now. Not what does "Methuselah" mean. If you impose a per
vamp rule that is a time limit. If you invoke a per turn rule that is
a time limit. And, if you invoke a as long as the card is in play rule
that is a time limit. Either way you have rewritten the card. Per
turn works just as easy as per vamp.

Also, you will note that Bribes seems to spell out what "Methuselah" is
meant to say. Any "Methuselah" that votes for the action gains one
blood. However, a "Methuselah" does not bleed and a "Methuselah" does
not vote. Therefore no one else can gain any blood. Wrong.
Therefore, if I have Five vamps with vote power each one can vote one
for and I gain five blood. (If we use the rule that is trying to be
imposed on Protected Resources now this would be the case). Or, as the
card says a "Methuselah" has to cast at least one vote for and none
against. This tells me that when the term "Methuselah" is used they
want us to understand that all minions are included in this. Does this
make since to any one else?

I agree if the card was in effect until the card holder bleed and could
lose no more than two pool, this would be a very over powered card.
However, as you have it interpretted it becomes very weak. It does
nothing to protect from the hated "winnie hoard" decks. I bleed you
fifteen times for one each.

I really don't see how you can say that it means per bleed. It doesn't
say that any where on it. So, how do you interpret it? I think the
inerpretation that is being imposed is just as wrong as any other. Per
turn, per bleed or for as long as the card is in play?

Last I would like to apologize to Mr Coupe I re-read my first message
and it sounded like an attack. Bad day and I wasn't feeling well. I
didn't mean to take it out towards you. That wasn't even what I really
did it just sounded that way to me.

After some time of newsgroup absence, I take the chance and jump right
into this discussion. :)

When this card (PR) first made appearance in my group, all players
animonously (sp?) read, interpreted and played it "per turn", without
dispute going on. It made perfect sense, and it was intuitvively.

However, in our league final that year, a clever Methuselah exploited
it to the full extend: He played Toreador with Masika, Alexandra,
Anneke and others. He put a PR in play; he also had HG-Blood Doll combo
and Art museum. So he could be bled for 2, but got them back during his
turn, net result: he was immune to bleeds. Next came Toreador Grand
Balls, and he called votes, namely KRC and Conservative Agitation. His
votes couldn't be blocked, and he had the political upper hand. Not one
of the other decks (bleed, stealth and bleed, vote) could stop him.

This led us to believe that "per turn" is too powerful.

What is the point of this story? Simple: I strongly believe that PR was
invented with "per turn" in mind. It meant to stop weenie bleeds,
during the change from Jyhad to VTES a number of anti-bleed changes has
been made (Archon Investigation, Elder Intervention, Justicar
Retribution and Protected Resources).
By the time the card came out, it was intuitively played "per turn", I
believe not only in our group (which was really large), but all around
the world. Even now, new players stumbling over PR play it that way.
After some time it was recognised that the card was broken. *But*, to
say now that it's always been meant to say "per bleed", and that that's
the most intuitively way to interpret it, is simply wrong.
So, the wording on PR now is errata, and not a clarification actually.
Why is it so difficult to just state that: PR was broken, the errata
fixed it.
As it is now, PR is a *bit* too weak. I wouldn't bother to make use of
it, and frankly, it's really no great use at all. It doesn't stop
weenies, you get ousted at the same pace. However, I agree that the
original version was too strong (broken) and needed fixture.

(snipped)

>
> Why not ask has this Methuselah bleed me for 2 pool already? Yes,
then

> interpretation. And the last member on that night was convinced by us
> to play it that way even though he wasn't in agreement. And it did
> make for a long game with 3 combat decks and 1 vote deck.

Well, I like the idea of having a good and solid set of rules for
international and tournament play. LSJ is doing a good job here.
However, I seldom agree with individual rulings and errata, but I
accept them, because it's played the same by everyone then. (At least
in official events.)

I will never stop shaking my head about some of the erratas
(Wake,RtI,...hey that's all I can think off at the moment; I must have
taken to like the others! : ), and some other I find totally ok after
some thinking about it (Fame, Pulled Fangs, ToRIII, etc.).

Players will always dislike some of the rules/erratas. That's ok, it's
the overall game-balance and playability that counts.

Thanks for giving me the opinion to voice my thoughts once more,

Carl

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
ravnos...@my-deja.com wrote:
> I don't see stating Methuselah on the card to limit each
> vamp to 2 bleed. That would have been much more easily stated as no
> Vamp can bleed for more than 2.

More precisely: no *minion* can bleed for more than two pool (per bleed
action).

But it is equivalent with the concept of what a "Methuselah's action"
is (i.e., an action taken by one of the minions under the control of
that Methuselah).

The fact that the information could have been conveyed in a more readily
understood format doesn't change the situation. Many cards could've been
worded better.

> I am not trying to be an @$$. But,
> when you use a word that is associated with the player then you it

> should limit the player not each of the minions individually. Does
> anybody understand what I am trying to say or am I in left field all by
> myself?

It is limiting the (other players): each of their bleeds against you
can cause no more than a loss of two pool.

The alternative (involving limiting the player) would be to limit
all of each players bleed to a total of two pool for as long as
PR stays in play.

Adding an artificial "per turn" to the effect is only possible via
errata, and such errata has not been (and will not be) issued.

None of the cards requires you to remember the extent to which events
have accumulated, no.

Some cards require you to remember whether such-and-such has (as a
single event) happened (typically "since your last turn"):
Compel the Spirit, Donatien, Lextalionis, Sixth Tradition, and
The Treatment.

And some cards require you to remember "state" information
without the use of counters or other in-play indicators:
Ablative Skin, Betrayer, Praxis Seizure: X, etc.

But none require you to remember if such-and-such has happened to
such-and-such a degree.

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
carlos_...@my-deja.com writes:

>When this card (PR) first made appearance in my group, all players
>animonously (sp?) read, interpreted and played it "per turn", without
>dispute going on. It made perfect sense, and it was intuitvively.

It's not particularly intuitive to me. I have to say, when I first
saw the card, it never crossed my mind that it meant anything except
a limit of 2 pool per bleed. The word "turn" doesn't appear anywhere
on the card!

I've noticed a lot of players (myself included) have a tendency at times
to read into a game rule or card what we want it to say. I can
sympathize when it happens to someone else. It does tend to make for
some annoyance when the mistake is pointed out and folks still cling to
the thing they want, advancing all manner of arguments in its support.
In most cases, I suspect that if someone who knew better had illuminated
the point for these people when they first encountered the rule or the
card, it wouldn't have provoked _nearly_ as much resistance as it does
after they'd gotten used to it.

Fred

I agree here. If a ruling (or errata) would be available to players
early on in their VTES-career, they'd just say "oh, I guess I played it
wrong last night, let's play it the right way from now on."

It's only when things are being played for years (wrong or right), and
then suddenly changed, that players say "how stupid, we play it this

It's not a matter if something is right or wrong, it's about how to

reasons.
